Today we're deciding: Pick a destination for the winter cabin weekend.
For this simulated decision, I’ll treat the following setup as the shared facts.
Options:
A) Lakeside Cabin in Adirondack Mountains — cost per person: $280; travel time hours: 3.5; amenities: fireplace, hot tub, lake access (+ Scenic lake views with relaxing hot tub; − Longer travel time compared to other options)
B) Mountain Lodge near Whiteface Ski Resort — cost per person: $300; travel time hours: 2.5; amenities: ski-in/ski-out, sauna, communal kitchen (+ Direct access to winter sports and ski resort; − Highest cost within budget, less privacy)
C) Secluded Forest Cabin near Lake George — cost per person: $220; travel time hours: 3; amenities: wood stove, no cell service, hiking trails (+ Quiet, off-grid experience with nature immersion; − Limited modern amenities and connectivity)
D) Cozy Townhouse in Lake Placid Village — cost per person: $250; travel time hours: 2; amenities: full kitchen, Wi-Fi, nearby shops and restaurants (+ Convenient location with easy access to amenities; − Less rustic, more urban feel than cabins)
Context: Group size is exactly 5 people; Weekend trip from Friday afternoon to Sunday evening; Maximum budget per person is $300 including lodging and travel.
What matters most for our winter cabin weekend: cozy comfort, outdoor activities, travel time, or budget?
